applies_why: This judge text does not count any verse toward a broken link as an unanswered witness; it instead marks the Matthew 1:16 issue underdetermined and says the witnesses it mentions were answered.
quote: the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness' — whether the judge is counting a verse toward a broken link, or merely noting the point is underdetermined and that the witnesses were answered; the text does the latter.
why: The text says the witnesses were answered and does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, so it neither needs nor violates the quoted-sentence requirement.
